Stardew Valley is a wonderful game, but when you install large expansion mods like Stardew Valley Expanded, Ridgeside Village, and East Scarp, or download big mod collections with hundreds of custom items and visual packs, the game engine has to juggle a lot of extra work. Over time, that extra load can cause micro-stutters, slower loading, long save times, and high memory usage.

One of my main goals with Stardropium is to help people on basically any hardware, whether you play on an older laptop, a handheld like the Steam Deck, a MacBook, or a budget desktop, be able to enjoy some of the larger mods and collections that might have struggled to run smoothly before.

Stardropium looks at how the game and common framework mods handle background tasks, repetitive string creation, off-screen rendering, and save routines, and tries to clean up the unnecessary work. Everything here is meant to be safe and true to vanilla Stardew. I do not change gameplay rules, reduce texture resolutions, or delete game files.

[quote]
[b]Important Note on Mod Versions:[/b]
Because Stardropium interacts with various popular mods, [b]you must be running the newest, latest versions of Stardew Valley, SMAPI, and all your installed mods patched by Stardropium (other mods are fine to not update)[/b]. Using older or outdated versions of mods may lead to compatibility issues or errors.[/quote]
[quote]
[b]Upstream Pull Requests and Future Plans:[/b]
I view this as a community project, not a replacement for anyone's work. All of the optimizations in Stardropium that touch third-party mods are intended to eventually be submitted as official Pull Requests to the original mod authors. If and when an author reviews and merges an improvement into their own mod, I will remove that module from Stardropium so there is no duplicate code. My hope is to contribute useful improvements back to the community.[/quote]
[quote]
[b]Disclaimer and Feedback:[/b]
I am only human and I am not perfect. With hundreds of mods in the community and endless load orders, unforeseen edge cases can happen. If something looks odd, behaves weirdly, or if you encounter any issue, [b]please let me know in the Posts or Bugs tab, or message me directly on Discord (@arshia1381)[/b]. Constructive feedback is very welcome and helps me make this better for everyone.[/quote]

I do not want to make unrealistic promises or guarantee specific numbers because every computer and mod setup is different. Here is what I designed Stardropium to help with based on my testing:

[list]
[*][b]Big Modpacks and Expansion Collections:[/b] Caches repeated queries in heavy framework mods like Content Patcher, SpaceCore, and Alternative Textures so they do less redundant work each tick.[/*]
[*][b]Item Queries & Framework Mods:[/b] Builds a zero-allocation inverted index of all items and tags at launch, speeding up ALL_ITEMS queries (used heavily by machines, shops, and frameworks) up to 60x and eliminating up to 99.7% of temporary query allocations.[/*]
[*][b]TMX Map Tile Memory Overhead:[/b] Intercepts default rotation and flip properties during map parsing, avoiding up to 650 MB of duplicate string and dictionary allocations on large expansion maps (SVE, Ridgeside, East Scarp).[/*]
[*][b]Memory Overhead and Long Sessions:[/b] Tries to keep memory from climbing endlessly by running a safe heap compaction and memory trim while your character sleeps at night.[/*]
[*][b]Long Save Times and Timeouts:[/b] In heavily modded games, end-of-day saving can take so long that it causes timeouts or kicks players in multiplayer, or just leaves you stuck at a black screen. Stardropium uses buffered write streams and streamlined serializer passes to help speed up saving and avoid save-timeout disconnects.[/*]
[*][b]10-Minute Clock Ticks on Big Modlists:[/b] When the in-game clock advances 10 minutes, the game checks objects across all maps in your world. Stardropium fast-skips checking empty background maps with no objects or animals, reducing the hitch that can happen at 6:10, 6:20, etc.[/*]
[*][b]Busy Farms and Decorated Rooms:[/b] Skips preparing draw calls for furniture, animals, trees, and water tiles that are completely outside your screen.[/*]
[*][b]Camera Motion:[/b] Includes optional floating-point camera smoothing to reduce the subtle integer jitter when walking or riding diagonally on high-refresh displays.[/*]
[*][b]Developer API:[/b] Exposes high-performance zero-allocation tag and category lookups for other mod authors to build fast item logic.[/*]
[/list]

[size=3][b][color=#E9D5FF][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/52803/52803-1790331008-1124176954.png[/img][/color][/b][/size]

[b]Content Patcher Engine Optimizer[/b] - For: Content Patcher
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Content Patcher checks conditions and asset requests constantly. This module caches condition names to avoid allocating temporary strings on the heap, remembers file path checks so it does not query your storage drive repeatedly, and quickly skips assets that have no patches attached to them.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High (benefits almost every modded setup since Content Patcher is so widely used)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (performs the exact same checks, just cached)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Not yet made[/spoiler]

[b]Low Latency Garbage Collector[/b] - For: Vanilla / .NET Runtime
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Asks the .NET runtime to avoid major garbage collection pauses while you are actively farming, and instead encourages memory cleanup during sleep screens and map loading transitions where you will not feel it.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High (helps reduce random mid-game pauses)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High (uses standard .NET runtime settings)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Overnight Memory and Heap Compaction[/b] - For: Vanilla / System Memory
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Long play sessions with lots of mods can cause memory usage to slowly creep up. While your farmer sleeps at night, this asks the system to compact the heap and release unused working memory back to the operating system. It does not unload or delete textures.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High on longer play sessions or devices with 8GB RAM
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High (safe non-destructive memory trimming)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Initial Load Accelerator[/b] - For: Vanilla / Mod Startup
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Scans mod folders and reads content pack manifests in parallel during initial launch, which helps shorten the time spent waiting at the startup loading screen.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High if you have hundreds of mods installed
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High (only runs before the main title screen loads)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]High-Throughput Save Stream[/b] - For: Vanilla / Saving System
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Uses larger memory buffers when writing the save file to disk at night, helping the end-of-day save process finish faster and reducing save-timeout disconnects in multiplayer.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium (noticeable if saves take a while)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (produces the exact same save file)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]String Memoization[/b] - For: Vanilla / Memory Allocation
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] The game creates thousands of temporary text strings for coordinates, item IDs, and clock times. This keeps a small cache of commonly used strings and reuses them instead of generating new ones constantly.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Subtle (helps reduce general background garbage collection)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Item Query & ALL_ITEMS Fast-Resolver[/b] - For: Vanilla / Machine & Framework Queries
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] When machines, shops, or mods like Automate or Content Patcher search for items using ALL_ITEMS with tag or category filters, vanilla 1.6 instantiates every registered item into memory to test conditions. Stardropium indexes all tags and categories at startup, filters candidate IDs in O(1) time, short-circuits global conditions (season, weather, flags) in 0.001 ms, and lazily streams item creation so First/Random queries instantiate at most 1 item instead of thousands.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Very High (eliminates up to 99.7% of query allocations, 60x faster machine/shop scans)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (strict 1:1 parity with vanilla query logic and dynamic game-state conditions)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Spatial Collision Partitioning[/b] - For: Vanilla / Player Movement
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Organizes map obstacles into a spatial grid so player collision checks only test nearby objects rather than looping through every item on the entire map.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium (mostly helpful on very crowded farm layouts)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]SMAPI Reflection Fast-Path[/b] - For: SMAPI / Mod Calls
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] When mods use reflection to access game methods through SMAPI, this caches the method handles and delegates so repeated calls avoid slow lookup overhead.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium (depends on which mods you run)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Not yet made[/spoiler]

[b]Furniture Frustum Culling[/b] - For: Vanilla / Decorated Interiors
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] In heavily decorated houses or sheds with hundreds of items, the game normally prepares draw calls for all of them even if they are off-screen. This skips drawing furniture that sits outside your viewport.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High if you have densely decorated rooms
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (off-screen items look identical whether drawn or not)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Map Layer Batching[/b] - For: Vanilla / Large Maps (SVE, Ridgeside)
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Groups static map tile drawing passes together to reduce the total number of draw operations sent to your graphics hardware on expansive custom maps.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium to High (helpful on large outdoor maps)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Vegetation and Crop Frustum Culling[/b] - For: Vanilla / Outdoor Maps
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Skips draw calls for wild trees, grass tufts, and crops that are off-screen. Growth timers, crop states, and forage drops are completely untouched.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium (helpful on huge farms or dense forest maps)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Animal Frustum Culling[/b] - For: Vanilla / Farm Animals
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Skips sprite drawing and animation rendering for farm animals when they wander outside your current screen view.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium if you own many full barns and coops
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (animal logic and happiness are unaffected)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Lighting Surface Caching[/b] - For: Vanilla / Lighting
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Caches the lighting texture and avoids redrawing light maps when local light sources and in-game time have not changed.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Subtle to Medium
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Water Tile Wave Culling[/b] - For: Vanilla / Water and Beach
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Skips animated wave calculations for water tiles located outside your screen.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Situational (mainly relevant at the Beach or Ginger Island)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Camera Subpixel Viewport Smoothing[/b] - For: Vanilla / Camera
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Vanilla Stardew snaps the camera to whole integer pixels each frame, which can look jittery when moving diagonally or riding horses on high-refresh displays. This uses floating point smoothing for a cleaner camera motion.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium (visual smoothness improvement)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High (visual only; can be toggled off in GMCM if you prefer vanilla pixel snapping)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]10-Minute Clock Tick Optimization[/b] - For: Vanilla / In-Game Clock
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Every 10 in-game minutes, the game iterates over all locations in your world to pass time for machines, animals, and buildings. In heavily modded saves with over a hundred maps, checking and locking every empty map adds up. This module fast-skips checking background locations that have no objects, animals, or buildings, avoiding unnecessary lock contention and enumerator allocations across empty maps.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High on large modlists with many custom locations
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (empty maps execute 0 iterations in vanilla anyway)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Remote Location 15 Hz Simulation[/b] - For: Vanilla / Background Maps
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] The game normally updates all 50+ background locations 60 times a second even when you are nowhere near them. This slows down non-active map updates to 15 times a second to save CPU time while keeping timers, crop growth, and animal states normal.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High on large expansion setups with dozens of locations
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Background Location Update Staggering[/b] - For: Vanilla / Background Locations
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Staggers non-essential ambient timers on remote maps so they do not all run on the exact same frame.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Off-Screen NPC Animation Throttling[/b] - For: Vanilla / Villagers
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Lowers the animation update rate for villagers who are far outside your camera view, and restores full normal animation speed as soon as they walk on screen.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium in town or at festivals with many characters
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] High (NPC schedules and walking paths remain accurate)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]NPC Schedule Pathfinding Cache[/b] - For: Vanilla / NPC Schedules
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] At 6:00 AM, many custom NPCs calculate their daily routes at the same time. This caches calculated path nodes so identical walk paths do not need to be recomputed from scratch.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium at the start of the day
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Map Load and Property Cache[/b] - For: Vanilla / Map Warps
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Caches parsed map properties and tilesheet references to help reduce the slight stutter when warping between maps or entering buildings.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Medium
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]TMX Tile Property Optimization[/b] - For: Vanilla / SMAPI Map Loading
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] When loading TMX maps, SMAPI's loader assigns default "@Rotation" and "@Flip" properties with a value of "0" to every standard tile. In large modpacks with thousands of map chunks, this allocates millions of duplicate string and dictionary entries. This module intercepts 0-value defaults during map parsing, avoiding 150 MB to 650+ MB of unnecessary heap bloat while preserving all non-zero rotations and custom map properties.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High (saves substantial RAM on setups with SVE, Ridgeside, or East Scarp)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (tiles with 0 rotation and no flip render identically)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Asymmetric Co-op UDP Socket Expansion[/b] - For: Multiplayer / Co-op
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Increases the network UDP socket buffer from the vanilla 128 KB to 1 MB. This helps prevent packet drops and sudden disconnects when warping between crowded locations in multiplayer. It works on your end even if the other player does not have the mod.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High in co-op (does nothing in single-player)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High (does not alter packet data or game rules)
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Live Diagnostics and Telemetry HUD[/b] - For: Diagnostic Tool
[spoiler]
[b]What it does:[/b] Provides console commands (perf_status, perf_memory, perf_trim) and an optional in-game display to check frame times, draw calls, and memory usage in real time.
[b]Rough Impact:[/b] Low (it is a tool for monitoring, not an optimization itself)
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium[/spoiler]

[b]Rough Impact:[/b] High for mods that integrate with it
[b]Likelihood to work without issues:[/b] Very High
[b]Upstream PR Status:[/b] Built into Stardropium ([url=https://github.com/ArshiaS1381/StardropiumMod/blob/main/docs/API.md]API Documentation[/url])[/spoiler]


[size=4][b][color=#C084FC][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/52803/52803-1790331057-99268693.png[/img][/color][/b][/size]
[color=#581C87]----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/color]
You do not have to configure anything if you do not want to. The default settings are set up to work out of the box.

If you have [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu (GMCM)[/url] installed, you can press Escape in-game, click the options cog, and:
[list]
[*]Turn any specific module on or off at any time.[/*]
[*]Pick from ready-made presets like Maximum Smoothness, Battery Saver (for Steam Deck / laptops), or Vanilla Plus.[/*]
[*]Use a button to trigger an immediate memory trim.[/*]
[/list]
[b]Console Commands (type into the SMAPI console):[/b]
[list]
[*][b]perf_status[/b] - Displays active telemetry, how many draw calls were skipped, and memory stats.[/*]
[*][b]perf_memory[/b] - Shows a breakdown of RAM, GC heap, and cached data.[/*]
[*][b]perf_trim[/b] - Manually trims memory and flushes dormant caches.[/*]
[/list]
[b]For Mod Authors (Developer API):[/b]
Stardropium exposes a public C# API ([b]IStardropiumApi[/b]) allowing other mods to access our zero-allocation item index, category lookups, and fast query resolver. Full details and usage examples are available in the [url=https://github.com/ArshiaS1381/StardropiumMod/blob/main/docs/API.md]Developer API Documentation[/url].


[size=4][b][color=#C084FC][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/52803/52803-1790331072-788632704.png[/img][/color][/b][/size]
[color=#581C87]----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/color]

[b]Prerequisites:[/b]
[list]
[*]Stardew Valley (PC, Mac, Linux, or Steam Deck).[/*]
[*]The newest version of [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url].[/*]
[*]The newest versions of all your installed mods.[/*]
[*](Optional) [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu[/url] if you want to change settings in-game.[/*]
[/list]
[b]To Install:[/b]
[list]
[*]Download the mod file from the Files tab.[/*]
[*]Extract the [b]Stardropium[/b] folder into your [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b] directory.[/*]
[*]Start the game using SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]
[b]To Update:[/b]
[list]
[*]Delete your existing [b]Stardropium[/b] folder from your [b]Mods[/b] directory first, then place the new folder in.[/*]
[/list]
[b]To Uninstall:[/b]
[list]
[*]You can safely delete the [b]Stardropium[/b] folder at any time. It does not alter your save files or store permanent custom items.[/*]
[/list]

If this helps your game feel smoother or reduces lag on your PC, Steam Deck, or Mac, please let me know! If you got an improvement, feel free to upload screenshots or images of your results (frame pacing graphs, before/after FPS, or memory stats) in the Images or Posts tab.

If you encounter any bugs, weird visuals, or mod conflicts, please submit a report on the [b]Bugs[/b] or [b]Posts[/b] tab with a link to your SMAPI log ([url=https://smapi.io/log]smapi.io/log[/url]). You can also reach out to me directly on Discord at [b]@arshia1381[/b].
